schemeScope: Combined Ordinary scheme. PDF 12–13 Léamhthuiscint A (with the Paper 2 heading, the penalty note and mark boxes at its end); 14–15 Léamhthuiscint B; 16 Prós Ainmnithe (2A: Oisín i dTír na nÓg, Hurlamaboc); 17 Prós Roghnach (2B); 18–19 Filíocht Ainmnithe (3A, its closing note on PDF 19); 20 Filíocht Roghnach (3B); 21 the same closing note for 3B and the modified marking (SMM). PDF 1–11 belong to Paper 1; 22–24 hold the SMM tables and blank pages.
reviewMethod: Every paper page (1–3 cover and instructions, 4–7 the two reading passages, 8–12 literature) and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page; each prompt and scheme slice is asserted against the PDFs by the builder.

nonPoolDecisions: Reading: all ten questions are required; each printed (a)/(b) part is a 5-mark practice card beside the whole question. Two-point items (“3 mharc + 2 mharc”, or Reading A 2(a)’s bare “5 mharc” with “An chéad rud atá ceart = 3 mharc; an dara rud atá ceart = 2 mharc”) are order-dependent (first correct point 3, second 2) and stay whole at 0/3/5; single answers allow 0/5, or 0/3/5 where the scheme prints a 3-mark partial answer (“= 3 mharc”, or “Gan ach cluiche amháin luaite, bronn 3 mharc air.”).
Reading language: “Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 5 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh” is one deduction from each 50-mark passage total; cards state it without applying it inside a part.

Prescribed prose (2A): (a) Oisín i dTír na nÓg is a summary that must cover five printed points (i)–(v), and (b) Hurlamaboc one question; the scheme prices both as five points (three at 7 = 5 + 2, two at 2 = 1 + 1) and never per printed point, so each is one 25-mark card and Oisín’s points are not carded apart (a per-point tariff would have to be invented).

Prescribed poetry (3A): each poem is a whole 25-mark card with its printed tariffs ((a) Mo ghrá-sa (idir lúibíní): (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9; (b) An tEarrach Thiar: (i) 8, (ii) 8, (iii) 9) and one 0–4 Gaeilge deduction; every printed sub-question is also a practice card. An tEarrach Thiar (i) prints four questions (a)–(d) at 2 each: each is its own practice card, and (i) keeps 0/2/4/6/8.
Optional prose (2B) and optional poetry (3B) stay whole: the text is open content chosen by the candidate. 3B(a) asks for a modern poem written by a woman and 3B(b) one written by a man.
Choice is not a route: Ceist 2 and Ceist 3 are each A or B; each printed question is one card carrying the printed choice and “Freagair (a) agus (b) anseo.”; no combination cards.
Literature language: “Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 4 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh” is one deduction from each 25-mark question, never inside one sub-question.
sourceFindings: Paper 2 = 200: Ceist 1 reading 100 (A Rory McIlroy - Galfaire na Bliana 2014 50, B Hillary Clinton agus Rás 2016 chuig an Teach Bán 50; ten questions at (a) 5 + (b) 5 each), Ceist 2 prose 50 (A Prós Ainmnithe: (a) Oisín i dTír na nÓg 25 + (b) Hurlamaboc 25; or B Prós Roghnach: (a) an optional folk tale 23 + title 2, (b) an optional novel extract 23 + title and author 2), Ceist 3 poetry 50 (A Filíocht Ainmnithe: (a) Mo ghrá-sa (idir lúibíní) 25 + (b) An tEarrach Thiar 25; or B Filíocht Roghnach: (a) 25 + (b) 25). 2015 prints no film or play question.

The scheme’s text layer stores ten boxed headings with the page body (“Páipéar II (200 marc)”, “CEIST 1 (A + B) - LÉAMHTHUISCINT -100 marc” with no space before 100, “A – (50 marc)”, “B – (50 marc)”, the CEIST 2/3 and section boxes); the builder removes those exact strings (count pinned).

2015 prints no two-point note above either passage and no general literature note (“Níl sé i gceist …”), so each criterion carries its own scheme slice alone. The penalty note (“Nóta: Gearrfar pionós i ngeall ar iomarcaíocht. Léireofar an pionós …”) and the mark boxes close each passage, and the last part’s key ends before them.

The reading key heads two lists with a printed line, “Dhá rud as na rudaí seo a leanas:” (A 2(a)) and “Dhá phíosa eolais as na pointí seo a leanas:” (B 3(a)); A 3(a) prints one bullet carrying both points (“Tá tallann iontach aige agus bíonn sé sásta caint faoina chluiche = 3 mharc + 2 mharc”) with the rule “Bronn 3 mharc ar an gcéad phointe atá ceart agus 2 mharc ar an dara pointe atá ceart”; A 4(a), A 4(b), A 5(a), A 5(b) and A 1(b) print 3-mark partial answers. All are lifted as printed.
The paper prints Reading A’s title with a hyphen (“Rory McIlroy - Galfaire na Bliana 2014”), the scheme with an en dash; cards show the paper’s print.

Oisín i dTír na nÓg and Hurlamaboc print the same key, word for word: “5 phointe eolais: 7 marc an ceann ar thrí phointe eolais agus 2 mharc ar an dá cheann eile. (7 marc = 5 mharc ar lomphointe eolais agus 2 mharc ar fhorbairt) (2 mharc = 1 mharc ar lomphointe eolais agus 1 mharc ar fhorbairt)”, with no sample points. 2B(a) and 2B(b) price “7 marc ar an gcéad dá phointe eolais, 5 mharc ar an tríú pointe eolais agus 2 mharc ar an dá cheann eile” (23) and the title 2 (2B(a) “Teideal an scéil bhéaloidis = 2 mharc”; 2B(b) title 1 + author 1); 2B(a) adds a “Treoir:” that the answer must treat both the kind of person and the main events. The scheme restates each question before its key; cards carry the key alone.

Mo ghrá-sa (idir lúibíní) (i): the paper prints “Cad is téama don dán Mo ghrá-sa (idir lúibíní) (thíos), dar leat?”; the scheme prints it without “(thíos)”. The card’s question is the paper’s print; the scheme slice is lifted as printed.

Each literature answer ends with “[Gaeilge lochtach: 0 - 4 a bhaint den iomlán a gnóthaíodh.]” (eight, word for word); each card carries it as the deduction criterion. The closing note “Nóta: Caithfidh an Scrúdaitheoir an marc don Ábhar …” is printed after 3A (PDF 19) and after 3B (PDF 21); it is examiner procedure, not on any card.
No 2015 Ordinary card existed before this review; the 48 cards are new.
